extracted.intended_audience: researchers in machine learning considering self-nomination as NeurIPS 2025 reviewers or area chairs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility criteria for researchers who want to self-nominate as reviewers or area chairs (ACs) for NeurIPS 2025, including publication, citation, and prior reviewing/AC service thresholds and procedural notes about selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need to meet all of the listed criteria; you should ideally meet several of them. The criteria should not be taken in a very strict sense and a free-form text box is provided to justify readiness if your background does not fit the criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NeurIPS recognizes diverse backgrounds and may accept reviewers/ACs who do not strictly meet every criterion; use the free-form justification to explain non-standard qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection is capacity-driven and possibly randomized
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the volume of self-nominations and the needs of the conference, NeurIPS may invite only a random subset of eligible candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not being selected in a given year does not imply you are unqualified; consider re-applying in future years because the pool and needs change year-to-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate existing reviewer acceptance when applying to be an AC
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have accepted an invitation to be a reviewer but want to self-nominate as an AC, indicate in the form that you previously accepted being a reviewer so organizers can remove you from the double role if selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer role is considered the most crucial role; if you are not selected as an AC, organizers encourage you to remain a reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and track allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The main track and the Datasets & Benchmarks (D&B) track recruit reviewers and area chairs together this year; selected individuals will be allocated to either the main track or the D&B track afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying does not lock you to a specific track; assignment will be decided after selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Hold a Ph.D. in a relevant field
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold a Ph.D. in a relevant field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a general indicator of domain expertise; absence of a Ph.D. can be explained in the free-form justification if other qualifications support readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: First-author publications (>=2 in past 5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Published at least 2 papers as first author in the past 5 years in any conference/journal from the listed venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues listed (REVIEWER_VENUE_LIST): NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, ICCV/ECCV, ACL, EMNLP, WACV, COLM, CoLLAs, RLC, AISTATS, KDD, IJCAI, AAAI, COLT, ML4H, CHIL, TMLR, JMLR. Meeting this threshold signals recent first-author research activity; other publication patterns may be considered with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Receive citations on first-authored papers (>=10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Received at least 10 citations on your first-authored papers (in relevant fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a quantitative signal of community impact for your first-authored work; citation counts should be interpreted in the context of subfield norms and career stage and can be discussed in the free-form justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Prior reviewing experience (>=2 consecutive times)
rubrics_metrics.description: Served as a reviewer at any conference/journal in REVIEWER_VENUE_LIST for at least 2 times in a row.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated reviewing for relevant venues indicates familiarity with peer-review practices; consecutive service is emphasized but not strictly required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Authorship on peer-reviewed papers (>=4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be an author on at least 4 peer-reviewed papers (this can include non-archival venues like workshops) on relevant topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts workshop and non-archival venues toward the total; intended to ensure sufficient exposure to peer-reviewed research in the area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair (AC) criterion: Last-authored papers (>=5 in past 5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 5 last-authored papers accepted at AC_CONF_LIST in the past 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues listed (AC_CONF_LIST): NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, ICCV/ECCV, ACL, EMNLP, KDD, COLT. Last-authorship is used as a proxy for senior/mentoring role and sustained leadership in a line of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair (AC) criterion: Total accepted papers in area (>=10)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 10 papers accepted at AC_CONF_LIST in the area of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric measures broader publication footprint in the area; counts across the AC_CONF_LIST venues and is separate from the last-authored threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair (AC) criterion: Prior AC service (>=2 consecutive times)
rubrics_metrics.description: Served as an AC at any conference in the AC_CONF_LIST at least 2 times in a row.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated AC service demonstrates experience with managing review processes; consecutive service is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair (AC) criterion: Prior reviewer service (>=5 consecutive times)
rubrics_metrics.description: Served as a reviewer at AC_CONF_LIST at least 5 times in a row.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive prior reviewing in the target venues is expected for AC candidates to ensure familiarity with the review community and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural: How to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are willing to self-nominate to serve as a reviewer or AC for NeurIPS 2025, fill in the provided form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post includes links to the application form(s) for reviewer self-nomination and for AC self-nomination; follow the form and indicate any relevant prior commitments (e.g., accepted reviewer invitations).
